scope: Read-only analysis plus isolated no-network/no-database fixtures. No shared runtime or repository test file was changed.

isolated composed-app witness observed exact order: schema, project bootstrap, all-project schemas, prompt sync, shared tables, production composition

evidence: celery_app.py does not register or invoke initialize_default_project_schema

an isolated Celery plus workflow_graph_smoke_local import, with the unrelated SQLite cache replaced and Engine.begin/connect fail-fast guards installed, made zero guarded DB calls
ensure_project_schema_ready exists for direct scripts but repository search found only four explicit callers; it is not a universal CLI boundary

checks.minimum_follow_up: Define and test one explicit Celery worker-start initialization boundary with production failure propagation, and require every DB-using CLI entrypoint to invoke the existing project bootstrap/preflight or a shared CLI wrapper. Do not restore import-time DDL.

evidence: build_run_store and build_compiled_graph_store remain the only configuration/failure owners
fail_closed=false returns the corresponding in-memory store
compiler, runtime and handoff lazy fields remain unset when the builder raises, and a later first operation retries
a selected in-memory fallback is cached for the service lifetime and does not silently switch back to SQL
checks.preserved_semantics: First requested SQL effect fails closed or selects the configured memory fallback. Fail-closed initialization is retryable on a later operation; selected fallback remains process-lifetime sticky and SQL is reconsidered only after reconstruction/restart.
checks.ceiling: No live SQL outage/recovery was exercised.

checks.scope: single service instance in one process
evidence: WorkflowGraphCompilerService, WorkflowGraphRuntimeService and WorkflowGraphHandoffStore each own an RLock around check-build-assign
24 calls across 12 threads produced one builder call and one shared resolved object for each service
checks.preserved_semantics: Within one service instance, initialization is serialized; a successful builder result is published once. A throwing builder publishes nothing, so a waiting or later caller may retry.

evidence: the RLocks are instance-local and process-local
default schema and compiled store DDL use IF NOT EXISTS
checks.not_proven: Multi-worker/process racing, PostgreSQL DDL lock behavior, partial initialization, and recovery after concurrent DDL failure were not exercised without a live database.
checks.minimum_follow_up: Add a disposable-PostgreSQL multi-process acceptance test or a single authoritative migration/startup owner before claiming cross-process preservation.
